title: Katsu Curry
subtitle: crisp breaded chicken cutlet with mild Japanese curry sauce
excerpt: Katsu curry pairs a golden breaded chicken cutlet with a thick, mild Japanese curry sauce. The cutlet is pan-fried until deeply crisp, sliced diagonally, and served over rice with the sauce poured over. A popular dish in Japanese homes and restaurants worldwide.
sourceNotes: Katsu curry combines Japanese curry sauce with tonkatsu (breaded, deep-fried pork or chicken cutlet). The dish became popular in Japan in the mid-twentieth century and is now a staple of Japanese school canteens and casual restaurants. Japanese curry restaurants in Britain helped popularise it from the 1990s onwards.

content.text: Katsu curry has two components: the breaded cutlet and the curry sauce. Both can be made at the same time. The sauce takes 20 minutes to build, which is about as long as it takes to bread and fry the chicken. Make the sauce first, then fry the cutlets while the sauce simmers.

items.prepNote: use 3 tbsp Japanese curry roux if available -- replaces spices and thickener
for the sauce -- use a separate portion

content.text: Make the curry sauce: fry the onion and carrot in 1 tablespoon of oil for 10 minutes until soft. Stir in the spices and cook for 1 minute. Add the flour and stir to coat. Pour in the stock gradually, stirring to avoid lumps. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Blend or pass through a sieve for a smooth sauce.
Set up a breading station: three shallow bowls -- flour, beaten egg, breadcrumbs. Season the flour with salt.
Coat each chicken fillet in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Press the crumbs on firmly.
Heat 2cm of oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Slice the cutlets diagonally into strips. Serve over steamed rice with the curry sauce poured alongside or over the top.

items.cause: Cutlet not properly dried before breading, or oil not hot enough
items.fix: Pat the chicken dry with kitchen paper before flouring. Make sure the oil is hot enough -- a breadcrumb dropped in should sizzle immediately.

content.text: Katsu curry is one of the most popular dishes in Japan. The crisp cutlet and the mild, glossy curry sauce are a perfect pairing. In Japan it is often served in school lunches. The dish has also become a fixture of Japanese restaurants around the world.
